artifacts.summary: Verified 444-occurrence inventory across 40 non-specs files partitioned 441 rename / 3 keep, with the 26-identifier Lean rename map, the paper-anchor decisions (def:frame#Saturation, cor:saturation-finite) with pre-computed checksums, gate couplings (C15, typst-sync-check, #guard_msgs), and measured baselines.

Three-phase plan (baseline capture, one atomic sentinel-guarded rename verified by a single detached guarded build, documentation coherence) for renaming the fourth task-frame axiom Spherical to Saturation across 40 files.

memory_candidates.content: Planning a tree-wide rename in a Lean 4 repo: when the renamed symbol lives in a root module that essentially every other module transitively imports (e.g. FormalSystem/Semantics/TaskFrame.lean, ~646 dependents), Lean's whole-file-hash invalidation makes EVERY verification build a full rebuild -- including a docstring-only touch. Do not decompose into N phases each ending in a build; plan one atomic edit followed by one detached guarded build, and split checkpoints by COMMIT rather than by build. Second reusable move: when a rename has a semantic carve-out ('rename the axiom name, keep the weaker standard condition'), first measure whether the keep-set collapses to a single distinguishable token. If it does, the partition becomes a sentinel-guarded global substitution with a mechanical post-condition (grep count == N) instead of hundreds of per-occurrence judgment calls -- the post-condition, not the inventory, is then the gate, so it catches a miscount in the plan's own figures. Third: irregular derivations of the stem (sphericality -> saturation, not saturationity) must be handled in a dedicated pass BEFORE the global substitution.
